eyedoc.foot: How the list was made: 6 Instagram searches (optometrist, eye doctor explains, ophthalmologist, optometrist glasses tips, eye doctor reacts, eye care tips doctor). About 500 posts collected, 363 Reels passed the 12-month and 3,000-view filter. 36 cover frames checked for talking to camera; skits, POV gags, simulations and b-roll removed. 14 doctors and practices checked against their last 20 Reels. Non-US and non-doctor accounts removed. Top 14 by score kept.

insights.text: Self-tests broke out hardest: the eye-teaming finger test at over 27,000x and the finger light check at 277x. A check viewers can do on the spot earns saves and shares.
insights.title: A test they can try now

insights.text: A doctor asking one either-or question, blind without your glasses or need them and skip them, hit 1,229x in 12 seconds. Short, one idea, comments as the poll. Strong fit for Anna.
insights.title: One relatable question

insights.text: Few eye doctors talk about frames and fit, yet Larchmont's frame care Reel hit 858x and Inna Lazar's fitting Reel 25x. Room for Anna, as long as it stays general education with no diagnosis and no health claims for frames.
insights.title: Frames are open ground

eyedoc.label: Eye doctor creators
eyedoc.rules:
- Anna speaks as an eye doctor: general education only, no diagnosis, always point to an in-person eye exam.
- No claims that frames or lenses treat, prevent or protect against any condition (including blue light claims).
- Cite a statistic only if Noon Shop has the source in hand.

fit.foot: How the list was made: 7 Instagram searches (glasses for round face, glasses for wide face, low nose bridge glasses, glasses sliding down nose, how glasses should fit, glasses face shape guide, frame size glasses too big). 577 posts collected, 565 not already in other topics, 278 Reels passed the 12-month and 3,000-view filter. Non-US, sunglasses-only and off-topic posts removed. 16 creators and brands checked against their last 20 Reels. Top 14 by score kept.

insights.text: The two biggest breakouts are about glasses sliding down the nose: a front-desk clip at 3,046x and a nose-pad fix at 1,179x. Every glasses wearer has felt it. A frame that stays put is the answer Noon Shop can show.
insights.title: Slipping is the top fit pain

insights.text: Memori's wrong fit vs right fit (129x) and Yuzu's fitting method (83x and 59x) show the payoff on a real face. Small fit-focused brands, small accounts, big multiples.
insights.title: Before and after sells fit

insights.text: The guides that broke out talk about bridge, eye size and features, not just round vs square: KayTran 78x, Tom Sasso 39x. A generic face-shape chart from a big account only reached 5x. Detail is Anna's lane.
insights.title: Go past the face-shape chart

fit.label: Fit and face shape
fit.rules:
- Fit claims only for what the frame was designed for (bridge, width, size). Never say a frame fits everyone.
- The answer to a fit problem is the right frame. Don't promote third-party fixes like nose pads or ear grips.
- Talk about appearance and comfort. Leave vision and prescriptions to an eye exam.

practice.foot: How the list was made: 7 Instagram searches (optical shop, optician, eyewear boutique, optometry office frames, new frames just arrived, optical store glasses, opticianlife). 541 posts collected, 211 Reels passed the 12-month and 3,000-view filter. Kept only accounts run by optical shops and practices; individual creators, non-US shops and Reels already in other topics removed. 12 shops checked against their last 20 Reels. Top 14 by score kept.

insights.text: Most of the top 14 are staff-made skits about life at the optical counter: pickups, phone calls, adjustments. Meyer Eyecare hit 326x and Blue River 139x in 10 seconds each.
insights.title: Behind-the-counter humor wins

insights.text: French Optical turned a frame that's too small (170x) and glasses sliding down the nose (111x) into a laugh. A ready-made angle Noon Shop can hand to the practices it sells to.
insights.title: Fit problems make great content

insights.text: Six shops with typical views under 3,000 broke out by 100x or more. A monthly Reel idea built on Noon Shop frames gives wholesale accounts content that sells and keeps Noon Shop on their walls.
insights.title: Small shops, big breakouts

practice.label: Optical practice (B2B)
practice.rules:
- Written for a practice to post under its own name. Tag Noon Shop frames; never present them as the practice's own brand.
- Customer humor stays kind. Never show real patient information.
- State lens and coating benefits only as the manufacturer states them.

tryon.foot: How the list was made: 7 Instagram searches (glasses try on, new glasses, which glasses should I get, eyeglasses haul, glasses for your face shape, glasses outfit, eyewear try on haul). 561 posts collected, 272 were Reels from the last 12 months with 3,000+ views. 21 eyewear creators and brands checked against their last 20 Reels. Non-US, sunglasses-only and off-topic accounts removed. Top 14 by score kept.

insights.text: The biggest breakouts from small eyewear brands are about fit: Greenwich Social Club at 244x and 191x on why glasses look wrong on your face, Covry at 30x on the smile test. That is Noon Shop's lane.
insights.title: Fit beats fashion for small brands

insights.text: The pick-one format keeps winning: 1 or 2, which pair is your favorite, comment your fav. Short, two to four frames, and the question does the work. It matches SORA concept 1.
insights.title: Ask them to pick

insights.text: Several of the biggest try-on view counts come with tiny like counts, a sign of paid boosting. They are marked Likely paid boost. Learn the format, not the numbers, and disclose gifted or paid frames.
insights.title: Watch the paid numbers

tryon.label: Frame try-on and picks
tryon.rules:
- If frames were gifted or paid, say so on screen and in the caption (#ad or Paid partnership).
- Never claim a frame fits every face. Talk about fit for specific features (low bridge, wide face, narrow face).
